title: looking for someone to mentor me in algo trading
author: itsmydarkpassenger
selftext: Hey, i am months into algo trading now, and my python strategies are profitable (backtested on tick data with actual spread - not OHLC), but still my MT5 demo backtesting gets disastrously failed. i have made more than 125 versions of the MQL5 file, but still the problem isnt solved. i genuinely want guidance, i am ready to pay for it but not gonna lie, i cant pay. i am stuck. i am a college student (3yrs into trading now), so my finances are very tight, but i am happily ready to put in all the work and effort to make it work. i would love to get mentored.

comments.author: RemoraEdge
comments.body:
Check the following

1) your python strategy must not use lookahead bias. It must only use known left facts   
2) it must be compatible with mt5 constraints and source data  
5) you must prove that it can actually do what you want it to do using real time data, not just ideas or labels. (This will take you months to do)

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Don't write a 126th version. You have two systems that disagree and you have never made them explain where, which is why 125 attempts produced nothing.

Have both emit a trade by trade log with the same columns: timestamp, signal bar, intended price, actual fill, size, exit reason. Run them over the identical window and diff. Find the first trade where they part company and only debug that one. Everything after it is downstream noise.

In my experience the first divergence usually lands in one of four places. Bar semantics, where python decides on a completed bar and the EA is evaluating intrabar, or the reverse. Symbol specs, where the broker's stop level or freeze level quietly rejects your stop and the EA carries on with a different trade than you think. Costs, where swap and commission exist in MT5 and not in your python model. And tick mode, because open prices only versus real ticks are not the same test.

None of that needs a mentor. It needs one aligned log and an afternoon.
